elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no affiliate assignment carve-out.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d) permits either party, including Customer, to assign to a successor to its business or assets on written notice without consent; this encompasses a merger successor.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d) permits Customer to assign to a successor to its business or assets on written notice without consent, including a successor arising from an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all of its assets.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d) permits Customer to assign to a successor to its assets on written notice without consent.

elements.element: Vendor must obtain Customer's consent before any assignment.
elements.evidence: Vendor may assign to a successor to its business or assets merely on written notice, without Customer's consent.

elements.element: Customer must not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment.
elements.evidence: For Vendor assignments requiring consent, Section 20(d) states that the other party's consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign this Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: There is no competitor prohibition, and the successor carve-out could permit assignment to a Customer competitor without consent.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right based on Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The rendered operative language grants no termination right arising from Customer's change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor without the other party's consent.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d) permits either party to assign to a successor to its business or assets on written notice.

elements.element: Customer must provide the other party with written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor-assignment right is expressly conditioned on written notice to the other party.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor without the other party's consent.
elements.evidence: The mutual language in Section 20(d) permits Vendor to assign to a successor to its business or assets on written notice.

elements.element: Vendor must provide the other party with written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor-assignment right is expressly conditioned on written notice to the other party.

elements.element: Any Customer assignment other than an assignment to a successor requires Vendor's written consent.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d) requires the other party's written consent for any assignment outside the successor carve-out.

elements.element: Vendor must not unreasonably withhold consent to another Customer assignment.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d) provides that the required consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Any Vendor assignment other than an assignment to a successor requires Customer's written consent.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d) requires the other party's written consent for any assignment outside the successor carve-out.

elements.element: Customer must not unreasonably withhold consent to another Vendor assignment.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d) provides that the required consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the mutual fallback and appropriately conforms Section 3(c) to avoid contradiction while retaining the separate restrictions on transferring, leasing, exporting, or sublicensing the Work. It does not achieve the preferred position because it omits the Customer affiliate carve-out and competitor prohibition and allows Vendor successor assignments without Customer consent. Drafting is generally clear, though “successor to its business or assets” is less transaction-specific than an express merger, acquisition, or substantially-all-assets formulation.
